title: Audit roles-roadmap orchestration failures and publish final completion report
description: After every remaining roles-system roadmap task and the CCL lifecycle correction are independently approved, publish the operator-requested full report explaining why MAP did not advance, route, review, rotate, and clean up this work more effectively. Reconstruct the durable timeline; distinguish deliberate safety gates from control-plane defects; identify manual interventions, approval-consumption gaps, terminal-versus-durable-state drift, over-eager rotations, review-routing friction, attempt-budget behavior, and startup topology effects. Link every claim to canonical evidence and end with implemented fixes, remaining risks, and measurable follow-up recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Report provides an evidence-linked timeline from TASK-277 approval through final approval of every roadmap and CCL lifecycle task, including manual hcom interventions and state transitions.

Root-cause analysis distinguishes intentional safety controls from defects or missing automation across intake, approval consumption, dispatch, review routing, context rotation, standby/cleanup, and operator attention surfaces.
Each identified orchestration failure names the affected component, observable impact, why existing controls did not prevent it, and whether it was fixed, deferred, or accepted.

Report measures completed tasks, attempts, review cycles, unnecessary sessions, operator approvals, and remaining blocked work from canonical SQLite/events/hcom evidence without inventing unavailable data.
Final recommendations are prioritized, bounded, and linked to implemented artifacts or explicit follow-up tasks; validators pass and the report does not become a competing source of project truth.
